messages.text: Middlesex beat Leicestershire Foxes to end 36-year List A trophy wait

metadata.summary: Middlesex ended a 36-year List A trophy drought by beating Leicestershire Foxes by 31 runs to win the Metro Bank One Day Cup in a low-scoring final at Trent Bridge.
metadata.content: Metro Bank One Day Cup men's final: Middlesex beat Leicestershire Foxes to end 36-year List A trophy wait | Cricket News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Metro Bank One Day Cup men's final: Middlesex beat Leicestershire Foxes to end 36-year List A trophy wait Ryan Higgins made a superb maiden List A hundred from 115 balls at Trent Bridge, playing a starring role as Middlesex ended a 36-year List A trophy drought by beating Leicestershire Foxes by 31 runs to win the Metro Bank One Day Cup in a low-scoring final By ECB Reporters’ Network Sunday 20 September 2026 21:20, UK Image: Middlesex's Ben Geddes lifts the One Day Cup trophy Middlesex ended a 36-year List A trophy drought by beating Leicestershire Foxes by 31 runs to win the Metro Bank One Day Cup in a low-scoring final at Trent Bridge. Ryan Higgins made a superb maiden List A hundred from 115 balls with Harry Duke (55) backing him up as their 135-run sixth-wicket partnership steered Middlesex from 71-5 to 231 all out after Foxes all-rounder Ian Holland took 5-36 and wicketkeeper Ben Cox held five catches. Higgins and Duke were making their first appearances for Middlesex in this year's competition. New Zealand international batter Nick Kelly hit an equally brilliant 103 (107 balls) to lead a Leicestershire fightback from 79-5 but it was not enough to haul his side over the line, Tom Helm (3-32) claiming his vital wicket in a superb late spell as the Foxes were bowled out for 200. metadata.summary: JJ Spaun said he played with a "huge chip on his shoulder" during his BMW PGA Championship win and used being snubbed by Team USA's Presidents Cup side as motivation for his Wentworth victory.
metadata.content: BMW PGA Championship: How JJ Spaun used Team USA snub for Presidents Cup as motivation for dramatic Wentworth victory | Golf News | Sky Sports Skip to main content BMW PGA Championship: How JJ Spaun used Team USA snub for Presidents Cup as motivation for dramatic Wentworth victory JJ Spaun claimed a two-shot win at the BMW PGA Championship; Spaun discussed missing out on Team USA's Presidents Cup side and why him and his wife are obsessed with Jeremy Clarkson after his debut victory at Wentworth By Ali Stafford at Wentworth Sunday 20 September 2026 20:12, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the final round of the BMW PGA Championship, where JJ Spaun claimed an impressive victory JJ Spaun said he played with a "huge chip on his shoulder" during his BMW PGA Championship win and used being snubbed by Team USA's Presidents Cup side as motivation for his Wentworth victory. Spaun became the first player since Byeong Hun An in 2015 to win the DP World Tour's flagship event on debut, posting a final-round 67 to claim a two-shot success over Rory McIlroy, Aaron Rai, Adam Scott and Manuel Elvira. Last year's US Open champion also won on the PGA Tour earlier this season at the Valero Texas Open and finished 10th in the Presidents Cup qualification standings, having also made his Team USA debut in the Ryder Cup last September. metadata.summary: England's Charlotte Heath secured her maiden Ladies European Tour title in dramatic fashion, holding off a host of challengers to claim victory at the La Sella Open in Denia, Alicante.
metadata.content: Ladies European Tour: England's Charlotte Heath bounces back from blowing big lead to claim maiden win at La Sella Open | Golf News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Ladies European Tour: England's Charlotte Heath bounces back from blowing big lead to claim maiden win at La Sella Open Charlotte Heath clinched her debut Ladies European Tour title at the La Sella Open, bouncing back after letting a four-shot lead disappear to finish two shots clear of the field; watch LET golf live on Sky Sports Golf Sunday 20 September 2026 21:09, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from day four of the Ladies European Tour's La Sella Open, where Charlotte Heath closed out a maiden victory England's Charlotte Heath secured her maiden Ladies European Tour title in dramatic fashion, holding off a host of challengers to claim victory at the La Sella Open in Denia, Alicante. The 24-year-old rookie started the final round with a four-shot advantage and, despite seeing her lead disappear during a tense Sunday afternoon, she held her composure to card a final-round 73 and finish at 10 under par, two shots clear of the field. After three weather-affected days, gusting winds continued to add an extra layer of difficulty, and set the stage for a thrilling finale at one of the LET's premier events.
